description: We are a team of five from Cluj-Napoca, Romania. We are students at Babeș-Bolyai University looking to have fun and challenge ourselves in this hackathon.
summary:
Firelock, a web tool, turns NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots from MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS into one harmonized fire history for firefighters, early-warning teams, land managers and scientists. The sensors differ: a MODIS pixel is about 1 km (larger towards the swath edge), a VIIRS pixel 375 m. One large fire fits in one MODIS pixel but covers several VIIRS pixels, so VIIRS would seem to see more fires when it only sees one fire in more pixels. We join touching pixels of the same pass into one fire, then merge same-day overlapping detections from other passes and satellites, so each fire counts once and its radiative power is never summed across passes. A zero-shot Amazon Chronos-2 time-series model forecasts fire counts and intensity per 0.5° cell for 24 months; future months appear on the map, marked as estimates.

The app shows monthly fires (2002-2025) on a globe with a time slider, a statistics panel (changes versus last month, year and average; seasonal chart; daily fires; biggest fire) and freehand area selection with a likely-cause panel (land use, season, news), in eight languages. A consistent, non-inflated record makes MODIS-only and MODIS+VIIRS years comparable, supporting early warning, planning and research.
details: FireLock is a web-based burning activity calendar for firefighters, emergency responders, land managers and scientists. A Python pipeline merges NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspot pixels into one fire per local day, so overlapping satellite passes aren’t counted twice, and turns 2002–2025 into monthly map tiles served by an nginx tile server in Docker. The app, built with React, TypeScript, Vite and MapLibre in eight languages, shows the fires of one month at a time with a statistics panel comparing each month to past months, years and the average. Users can also draw an area and get a likely cause from transparent keyword rules (based on OpenStreetMap land use, the season, earlier fires at the same spot, and local-language news found through self-hosted degoog search and LibreTranslate). For a creative look ahead, the Chronos-2 model forecasts fire activity for the next 24 months on an ordinary CPU and was checked against real 2025 data. The team weighed sensor resolution differences, missing years versus years with no fires, and privacy (no API keys, data kept local).
